note: Attacker-controlled 32-bit data offset for the MakerNote entry is read straight from the input EXIF buffer; it later becomes offset_mnote and anchors all Apple MakerNote reads.
The tainted MakerNote offset is stored in the ExifData private structure for later use by interpret_maker_note.
The raw EXIF buffer and its length are handed to the Apple MakerNote loader after the MakerNote entry data is identified as 'Apple iOS'.
Per-entry read size is computed from attacker-controlled format/components fields of the Apple MakerNote entry table.
Attacker-controlled data offset is taken from the MakerNote entry without any bounds check against buf_size; the missing validation allows dofs + dsize to exceed the input buffer length.
Destination buffer of dsize bytes is allocated, but the read source buf + dofs is never validated to lie within the input buffer.
dsize bytes are copied from buf + dofs; with a crafted entry offset the read extends past the end of the heap buffer, causing a heap-buffer-overflow read.
